title: Alert sensitivity and panel pruning for multitenant inference
content:
Context and intent:
This doc is a working plan for reducing alert noise and dashboard query costs across multi-tenant inference dashboards. Goal is to: 1) set sensitivity tiers that scale with traffic, 2) define panel eviction/pruning heuristics to keep dashboards cheap and useful, 3) tie traces to cache/latency signals so operators can quickly pinpoint cold-cache vs serving regressions.

Quick summary (one-liner):
Make alert thresholds and dashboard panels traffic-aware and cost-aware, and ensure traces are anchored to cache hits/misses and routing decisions.

Why this matters now:
- Token surge incidents expose expensive dashboards (many high-cardinality panels that run heavy queries every minute).
- Multi-model fanout and per-tenant variability cause lots of false-positive latency alerts.
- Operators need fast trace anchors that explain whether latency comes from routing/batching, KV cache misses, or model-side backpressure.

Proposed primitives (definitions):
- Panel eviction score (PES): composite score used to decide which dashboard panels to prune when query budget exceeded. PES = alpha * recent-query-cost + beta * staleness + gamma * inverse-operator-value.
  - recent-query-cost: 3-hour rolling estimate of query cost (USD or platform tokens) for panel.
  - staleness: time since last significant update to panel definition.
  - operator-value: subjective weight (1-5) assigned by owners; default 3.
  - alpha/beta/gamma: start with 0.5 / 0.3 / 0.2 and iterate.

- Traffic-decile alert thresholds: alerts should scale by tenant traffic decile (D0 highest traffic -> D9 lowest).
  - For latency P95 alert: threshold = baseline_p95 * (1 + 0.02 * decile_rank) for D0-D4; larger multiplier for D5-D9 to reduce noise.
  - For error-rate alerts: use both absolute and relative thresholds (e.g., absolute > 0.5% OR relative increase > 3x).

- Trace anchors (schema): (these are names, keep stable in SDK/instrumentation)
  - trace.tag:tenant_id
  - trace.tag:request_type (text/generation/embedding/re-ranking)
  - span:router.lookup -> annotate with chosen_model_version + route_policy
  - span:kv.cache -> attributes: cache_hit (bool), prefix_key, hit_latency_ms
  - span:batch.worker -> attributes: batch_size, seq_len_dist, gpu_id
  - span:model.exec -> attributes: quantized (bool), kernel_variant, token_rate

- Sampling strategy: severity-weighted adaptive sampling. Always sample 100% of spans that: cache_hit=false AND latency > p99_baseline OR error_code >= 500. For low-severity (no cache miss, latency < p95) sample 0.5% by default and 5% for top 2 deciles of tenants.

Dashboard design notes (operator-first):
- Master page: Incident quickstrip: 6 tiles (global token RPS, global p50/p95/p99 latency, %requests with cache miss, %requests routed to fallback). Each tile has a hover drill link to a tenant-slice view.
- Tenant slice: top 8 widgets only. Each widget must declare estimated query-cost in metadata. Panels beyond 8 are hidden behind an "expanded" toggle and use on-demand queries (not auto-refresh).
- Heatmap: per-tenant cache-warmth (session-warmth index) with deciles. Compute session-warmth as fraction of requests within tenant where prefix_cache_hit=true over last 30m.
- Bucketed latency panels: show latency broken by cache_hit vs cache_miss and by batch_size buckets so operators can quickly identify whether bigger batches are causing P95 spikes.

Alert matrix (initial thresholds and rules):
- P0: Platform-wide token ingress drop > 10% sustained 3m OR global model exec errors > 2% sustained 5m. Notify on-call + #platform-ops.
- P1: Tenant p99 latency > baseline_p99 * 1.5 for > 10m AND cache_miss_rate > baseline + 5ppt. Pager to SRE on-call for top-3 decile tenants.
- P2: Tenant p95 latency deviation > baseline_p95 * 1.2 for > 30m. Create ticket, email owner.
- Noise suppression heuristics: only fire tenant-level pager if tenant is in top-4 deciles OR the deviation co-occurs with model.exec error spike.

Instrumention / implementation checklist (practical):
- [ ] Add cache_hit boolean to kv.cache span across runtime (runtime PR #912 reference).
- [ ] Add panel metadata field (estimated_query_cost_usd, owner, operator_value). Frontend change: dashboard metadata schema.
- [ ] Implement PES exporter job that computes Panel Eviction Score every 15m and writes to metrics store.
- [ ] Implement decile-based threshold engine in alerting service (config-driven).
- [ ] Introduce adaptive trace sampler with rules described above.
- [ ] Migration plan: 2-week trial on non-prod then opt-in for early adopter tenants.

Cost-control heuristics (how to prune without losing signal):
- Evict panels with PES > threshold when monthly query budget for signal tier reached. Eviction is soft: panels are hidden from auto-refresh and moved to archived view for 30d.
- Convert heavy panels (long JOIN/aggregation) to on-demand queries or precomputed rollups at 5m resolution.
- Tag high-cardinality panels (tenant x model x prompt-template) and require explicit owner approval to keep them.

Open questions / tradeoffs to discuss:
- How do we quantify 'operator-value' objectively? Proposal: 2-week voting window across operator teams, then use median weight.
- What is acceptable sampling delay for rollups vs live panels? Precompute some heavy aggregations with 2m delay to avoid expensive live queries.
- Should low-traffic tenants be entirely excluded from certain panels to cut cost? (privacy / completeness tradeoffs)

Investigations & notes to self (raw):
- Noticed a pattern where p99 latency spikes correlate with cache_miss_rate rising ~20ppt 5-7m earlier. Need a synthetic probe that sweeps prefix-key space to estimate warmth.
- Slack thread: OBS-thread #cache-warmth (see linked_artifacts) has customer examples.

Implementation timeline (rough):
- Week 0-2: schema changes (span attributes + panel metadata). Runtime and dashboard PRs.
- Week 3-4: PES exporter + basic eviction UI + decile threshold engine skeleton.
- Week 5-6: adaptive sampler rollout + trial on staging.
- Week 7-8: opt-in pilot for 10 internal tenants + iterate thresholds.

Owner / contacts:
- Doc owner: Priya Desai (eng-observability).
- Runtime instrumentation lead: Marco Nguyen.
- Dashboard owner: Ava Chen.
- SRE escalation: Liam O'Connor.

Notes for follow-ups: attach SQL snippets for cost estimation, add example Grafana panel JSONs to the confluence page, and schedule a 60-min working session with platform and SRE to reconcile decile boundaries.

End of doc (working).
